equal.e: From Middle English equal, from Latin aequālis.
equal.g: The same in one or more respects.

equality.e: Borrowed from Middle French equalité (modern French égalité), from Latin aequālitās, aequālitātem. By surface analysis, equal + -ity.

equip.e: From French équiper (“to supply, fit out”), originally said of a ship, Old French esquiper (“to embark”); of Germanic origin, most probably from Old Norse skipa (“to man (a ship)”), from Proto-Germanic *skipōną (“to ship, sail, embark”).
equip.g: To supply with something necessary in order to carry out a specific action or task; to provide with (e.g. weapons, provisions, munitions, ri

equipment.e: From equip + -ment, or from French équipement.
equipment.g: The act of equipping, or the state of being equipped, as for a voyage or expedition.

equity.e: From Middle English equitee, equytee, from Old French equité, from Latin aequitās (“uniformity; impartiality; fairness”).
equity.g: Fairness, impartiality, or justice as determined in light of "natural law" or "natural right".

equivalent.e: From Latin aequivalentem, accusative singular of aequivalēns, present active participle of aequivaleō (“to be equivalent, have equal power”). By surface analysis, equi- + -valent. Mostly displaced native Middle English efenmete.
equivalent.g: Similar or identical in value, meaning or effect; virtually equal.
